task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-06-19, in the area of play-type labeling and data quality):
Opponent next-possession PPP after you run play X is large enough to drive AVOID labels; own-sequence lags similarly matter.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: Is the opponent next-possession PPP shift after play X large enough to change AVOID labels beyond sampling noise?
Do own-sequence lags (previous own possessions or play types) have effects on PPP that survive controls?
How can sequence effects be separated from confounding by game state, lineup, defensive quality and outcome-derived possession boundaries?
What sample size, shrinkage and multiplicity control are needed at play-type x team level?

historical_evidence.finding: Opponent action T -> your offense T+1 with defense-matched 8x8 cells: 3/64 FINDING cells survived both matchings (SPOT_UP->TRANSITION ATT=-0.085; POST_UP->TRANSITION -0.083; PNR->DRIVE -0.058), also surviving a prev_made control. PULL_UP->DRIVE was dropped as a defense-quality confound. Most of the 64 cells were null. Used BH-FDR, placebo and free-throw cleaning.

Superstar sequential suppression: PUTBACK was the top suppressor for 6+ stars (e.g. D. Mitchell 1.178 to 0.884, n_after=95). No multiplicity correction; n_after was 32-95 in several cells; min n_after=30. No validation recorded; flagged DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY risk.

Superstar suppression profiles including sequential triggering: rank-1 suppressor varies across players (e.g. Jokic after opp POST_UP -0.0675, SE 0.05, n=480). Rank-1 deltas were mostly within 1-2 SE, with no multiple-comparison control; an OTHER artifact was flagged.

Net-swing prototype (own PPP minus opponent next-possession PPP): top recommendation changed in 40/104 (38%) team-offense units across 52 playoff series; DRIVE median net swing -0.27 (negative 88%), POST_UP -0.22 (77%). Descriptive only; not evaluated against outcomes; uses in-series observed opp_next_PPP.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Ranking top suppressors per star from small post-trigger samples without multiplicity correction
failed_approaches.why: As recorded: no multiplicity correction; n_after 32-95 versus thousands of baseline possessions; failure mechanism unclear.
As recorded: deltas mostly within 1-2 SE with no multiple-comparison control; OTHER artifact flagged; verdict inconclusive.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Net-swing scoring with raw observed in-series opp_next_PPP as a basis for recommendations
failed_approaches.why: As recorded: not evaluated against outcomes. Descriptive only, so it does not show that the swings are causal or stable.

evidence_establishes: [prior work][prior work] (supported): a small number of opponent-previous-play to own-next-offense effects (about -0.06 to -0.085 PPP) survive defense matching, offense matching and a prev_made control, while most cells are null.

[prior work][prior work] (descriptive): swapping own PPP for net swing changes the top recommendation in 38% of playoff team-offense units, so the label is sensitive to the metric as computed, with raw in-series values.
evidence_does_not_establish: That the opponent next-possession PPP effect is causal or stable once confounding and multiplicity are handled; the 38% change comes from raw, unvalidated in-series numbers.
That the raw net-swing magnitudes (e.g. DRIVE -0.27) reflect an effect of play X rather than selection, such as the type of possession that follows turnovers, makes or misses, or game state.
Anything about own-sequence lags (the team's own previous possessions) as a driver of labels; no retrieved record tests that directly.
That any effect holds out of sample, in regular season data, or for the 2025-26 data.
Whether the effect is large enough to flip AVOID labels at a given sample size; no record evaluated label flips against a noise-only baseline.
own_inferences: The 3/64 surviving cells with ATT around -0.06 to -0.085 suggest true sequence effects are small and sparse, far below the raw -0.2 to -0.27 swings in [prior work][prior work]; the raw swings probably embed mechanical or compositional confounds (for example, the opponent's next possession starts after a make or miss, transition after a miss and so on).

Opponent next-possession PPP after play X is partly mechanical: the outcome of X (make, miss, turnover, rebound) determines the starting type of the next possession, so conditioning on X is conditioning on its outcome.
The question as posed, that the effect is large enough to drive AVOID labels, is probably only supportable for a few play-type pairs; for most labels the effect should be within noise.
Own-sequence lags are likely weaker still and likely to overlap with the opponent-lag effect (alternating possessions).
uncertainties: Definition of AVOID labels and thresholds is not stated in the task or retrieved records.
How [prior work][prior work] handled possession-start type is unknown.
Whether a 'large enough' size criterion has been defined (e.g. label flip rate versus a permutation null).
Data after 2026-04-13 (regular season) and 2026-06-21 (playoffs) is partial or incomplete at the question date.
I did not read the full records (read_family) or graph [source], so details such as [prior work][prior work] are missing.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history I might have treated the raw net-swing effect as a ready basis for labels. [prior work] show that only 3/64 matched cells survive, that raw swings were never validated against outcomes, and that small-n rankings without multiplicity control were inconclusive. The decision therefore moves from proceeding as posed to proceeding with changes: a matched, shrunk, multiplicity-controlled test with explicit label-flip criteria and own-lag handled separately.

blocking_constraints.text: Next-possession start type is mechanically determined by the outcome of play X (make, miss, turnover), so raw opponent next PPP is partly outcome-derived and must be conditioned on possession-start type.
Team x play-type cells will be small; label-level decisions need pooling or shrinkage.

prior_work.summary: Opponent previous play to own next offense has been tested ([prior work][prior work], supported for 3/64 cells). Descriptive net-swing scoring exists ([prior work][prior work]) but was not validated. Star-level suppression work was inconclusive or not a test. The specific claim that opponent next-possession PPP after play X is large enough to drive AVOID labels, and the own-sequence lag part, have not been directly tested in the retrieved records.

risks.text: Game state, lineup, defensive quality (PULL_UP->DRIVE was dropped as a defense-quality confound in [prior work][prior work]), pace and opponent strength confound sequence effects.
Play-type labels and points are derived from play-by-play outcomes; the next possession type depends on the outcome of X.
Possession starts after makes, misses and turnovers differ in baseline PPP (e.g. transition after turnovers), producing a mechanical sequence effect.
Many play-type pairs and lags are tested; [prior work][prior work] and [prior work][prior work] lacked correction.
n_after of 30-95 in prior work gave unstable estimates (SE 0.05 at n=480).
Selecting top suppressors or most negative cells inflates extremes (winner's curse).
Play-type mix and league scoring change across seasons; [prior work][prior work] flagged this risk.
Play-type labels derived from play-by-play may misclassify, including an OTHER artifact flagged in [prior work][prior work].
Using in-series observed opp_next_PPP to set labels evaluated on the same series is look-ahead ([prior work][prior work]).
Conclusions depend on a placebo design (e.g. shuffled or lead rather than lag) being appropriately built.

design.estimand: For each play type X, the adjusted average difference in opponent next-possession PPP (and separately own T+2 PPP) after X versus after a matched reference, conditional on possession-start type, plus the rate at which replacing own PPP with net swing (own PPP minus adjusted opponent next PPP) flips a play type's AVOID label relative to a noise-only permutation null.
design.unit: Possession pair (X possession, immediately following opponent possession), and for own-lag, the team's possession triple (own previous, own current).
design.sample: NBA 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoffs for development and estimation; 2025-26 regular season (complete 2026-04-13) as a pre-registered holdout. 2025-26 playoffs excluded until complete on 2026-06-21. Exclude garbage time, end-of-period possessions, free-throw-only trips, and OTHER-labeled possessions.
design.power: Compute SE by cluster bootstrap by game; require a minimum number of pairs per cell (e.g. n >= 300 per X x next-type) or hierarchical shrinkage; pre-state the minimum detectable effect (target about 0.05 PPP, in line with the -0.06 to -0.085 effects in [prior work][prior work]) and report cells below it as inconclusive.
design.controls: Match or regress on possession-start type (after make, miss, turnover), score margin, period and clock bucket, own and opponent team quality, defensive lineup and matchup, prev_made, season; mixed model with team and game random effects; treat own-lag and opponent-lag in the same model to separate their contributions.
design.falsification: Placebo using the possession two steps back or a shuffled order within game; negative control with outcome unrelated to X's type; check for effects in non-adjacent possessions; replicate the 3 [prior work][prior work] cells as a positive control; AVOID flip rate must exceed the permutation-null flip rate.
design.multiplicity: BH-FDR at 0.05 across all X x next-type and lag cells, with a single pre-registered primary family; report shrunk (empirical-Bayes) estimates instead of top-ranked raw cells.
design.decision_rule: Supported if adjusted effects exceed the minimum detectable effect in at least a pre-specified set of play types, survive FDR and the placebo, replicate in the 2025-26 holdout with the same sign, and the AVOID flip rate exceeds the permutation null. Rejected if adequately powered adjusted effects are below 0.03 PPP and flip rates are within the null. Otherwise inconclusive; own-lag claims need the same criteria separately.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API play-by-play files and the derived play-type possession graph as of 2026-06-19; freeze the extraction and labeling code version and hash; holdout is the complete 2025-26 regular season (from 2026-04-13); 2025-26 playoffs excluded as partial.
